name: AICapabilityCard
description: AICapabilityCard is a compact, reusable card for representing a single AI capability, model skill, or agent behavior. Each card pairs an origin chip (System Defined / Client Extended / User Configured / Experimental) with a bold title, a short description, and a layers footnote. Clicking the card opens a detail drawer with the capability's reasoning summary, confidence + trend metrics, autonomy boundaries, and knowledge inputs — making the agent's skills inventoryable and reviewable. A "View Full Details" footer link deep-links to a standalone capability page when configured.
intent: Compact card that surfaces a specific AI capability or model skill, with origin chip + Inspect affordance.

keyboard: Ensure keyboard focus order matches visual order

usage: A capability gallery or inspector needs an inventoryable view of agent skills
Capability origin (system / client / user / experimental) needs to be explicit
Capabilities need to be marked needs-review or disabled with a clear reason
doNotUse: A single binary toggle is enough — use ai-toggle
You need to show *what an agent did*, not *what it can do* — use ai-card-agent-reasoning
A long-form capability spec is needed — use a dedicated capability detail page
Do not invent dependency atomics — use bundled canonical sources
Do not hardcode brand hex — use AI tokens
Do not require an external AI UI package for agent implementations — use co-located TSX

gaps.reason: No Figma file, node, or Code Connect mapping in the spec or manifest.
No variants declared in manifest, source unions, or spec table.
No Guild semantic tokens declared in the manifest or extracted from TSX. Not guessed.
Manifest accessibility block is a generic placeholder, not a reviewed contract.
AI component has no schema-valid experienceMetadata (modes/behaviors/accountability). Not inferred.
